title: Elasticity: stress, strain, Young's modulus
examples: What is the difference between stress and strain?
How do I calculate Young's modulus?
What does the slope of the stress-strain graph tell us?

explain.say: Today we look at how materials stretch and break.
Stress is the force applied over an area.
Strain is the material's measure of deformation.

draw.text: Strain = Change in Length / Original Length

explain.say: The stress-strain graph shows these relationships clearly.
Young's modulus is the slope of the linear part of this graph.
If you pull a spring, the initial straight line tells you its modulus.

faq.q: What is the difference between Young's modulus and the material's strength?
faq.a: Young's modulus measures stiffness in the elastic region. Strength relates to the maximum stress before breaking.
asks: What does the slope tell me?
Is modulus the same as breaking stress?

faq.q: Can I use the stress-strain graph for any material?
faq.a: The graph is useful for many materials, but its shape changes depending on the material type.
asks: Does the graph look the same for metal and rubber?
When does the graph stop being linear?

faq.q: What happens after the material passes its elastic limit?
faq.a: After the limit, the material deforms permanently, meaning it will not return to its original shape.

faq.q: Does the units for stress and strain cancel out when finding Young's modulus?
faq.a: Yes, the units of stress divided by the units of strain give the correct units for Young's modulus.
asks: What are the units for stress?
Do I need to convert units for strain?

faq.q: Is the breaking stress the same as the yield stress?
faq.a: No, the yield stress is where permanent deformation starts. The breaking stress is where it actually fractures.

facts: Stress is calculated by dividing the applied force by the cross-sectional area.
Strain is a dimensionless quantity, meaning it has no units.
Young's modulus represents the material's resistance to elastic stretching.
The breaking stress is the maximum stress a material can withstand before failing.

quiz.say: A metal rod experiences a force of 100 newtons over an area of 0.01 square meters. What is the stress?
quiz.why: Stress is force divided by area, so 100 divided by 0.01 is 10000.

wrong.0: This suggests the force and area units cancel out completely.
wrong.2: This incorrectly divides the force by 100 instead of 0.01.
wrong.3: This mistake forgets to account for the small area value.

quiz.say: If a wire stretches from 2 meters to 2.2 meters, what is its strain?
quiz.why: Strain is the change in length divided by the original length, so 0.2 divided by 2 is 0.1.

wrong.0: This only calculates the change in length, ignoring the original length.
wrong.1: This incorrectly divides the change in length by the change in length.
wrong.2: This incorrectly uses the final length instead of the original length.

quiz.say: Which value best represents the material's stiffness in the elastic region?
quiz.why: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of stress to strain in the elastic region, which is the slope.

wrong.0: Strain is a measure of stretch, not the material's inherent stiffness.
wrong.1: Force is the input, but Young's modulus is a ratio describing the material.
wrong.3: Breaking stress is the maximum force, not a measure of initial stiffness.
